rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment must establish a strong multimodal anchor to calibrate the search. config_021 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) combines a well-established RNA encoder (scvi_n200), a powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), the more informative multiprofile setting, an expressive transformer aggregation, and a simple/robust concat fusion. This tests the core hypothesis that multimodal fusion with strong per-modality encoders yields high accuracy, while keeping the fusion strategy simple to isolate encoder and aggregation contributions. It provides a high-quality reference point: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can exploit by swapping individual components (e.g., scgpt, weighted fusion); if it underperforms, we learn which component to simplify. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the 10-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_021: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat → 72.1% acc), evidence is sparse. The most informative next step is a single-variable ablation from the current best to isolate the impact of one design choice. Config_039 changes only the fusion from concat to weighted, keeping all other settings identical. This directly tests whether adaptive weighted combination of RNA and image features (vs. simple concatenation) improves accuracy, which is a fundamental multimodal design decision. If weighted fusion helps, it confirms that modality weighting matters and opens a productive exploitation direction (e.g., weighted fusion combined with other changes). If it doesn't, we confirm concat is sufficient and can redirect exploration toward RNA encoder or aggregation choices. Under the 8-experiment remaining budget, this clean comparison maximizes information gain per experiment.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_021, config_039) establish that multimodal + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer achieves ~72.1-72.5% accuracy, with weighted fusion marginally preferred over concat. However, the RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) remains a major untested axis that could significantly shift performance. Question: config_007 tests scgpt as the RNA encoder while holding the other components at their best-known settings (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile). This directly isolates the effect of a more specialized single-cell foundation model on the RNA side. Why this is the best next step: With 7 experiments remaining, resolving whether scgpt outperforms scvi_n200 is critical because it determines which RNA-encoder family to exploit in subsequent runs. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a promising sub-space (e.g., config_014, config_023); if not, we confirm scvi_n200 and pivot to image-encoder or aggregation variations. This single experiment reduces the largest remaining source of uncertainty in the design space.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.7250) uses transformer aggregation with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion. We have only tested transformer aggregation so far; the effect of aggregation method is an important untested design axis. config_004 is a clean ablation: it holds all other settings at their best-known values (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, weighted fusion) and swaps transformer for avgpool. This directly tests whether the more complex transformer aggregation is contributing meaningfully or whether a simpler pooling suffices. Under a 6-experiment remaining budget, resolving this architectural question is high-value: if avgpool matches transformer, it confirms a simpler direction to exploit; if it lags, it validates transformer and narrows the search space, freeing later experiments to focus on image encoder or profile setting.

Evidence: The best config so far (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. All four completed experiments used imagenet_vit_l, so the image encoder dimension is completely unexplored. The RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) showed a massive gap (~0.20 acc), indicating encoder architecture is a high-impact choice. Question: Does resnet50 as the image encoder perform comparably or better than imagenet_vit_l when all other parameters are held at their best-known values? Why this is the best next experiment: config_013 differs from config_039 only in image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l), giving a clean single-variable comparison on the most important untested design axis. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving whether the image encoder is a binding constraint (or flexible) is critical for guiding the remaining budget efficiently.

Evidence: The top-5 experiments all use multiprofile, with config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) leading at 0.7250 acc. scvi_n200 is clearly the best RNA encoder (0.72 vs 0.52 for scgpt), imagenet_vit_l edges out resnet50 on accuracy, transformer beats avgpool, and weighted slightly beats concat. However, the profile setting (multiprofile vs singleprofile) is a major architectural dimension that has been completely untested. Question: config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + singleprofile + weighted) is a clean ablation of config_039 with only the profile setting changed, directly testing whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation pipeline is essential or whether a simpler single-profile fusion can match or exceed it. Why this is the best next experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, resolving whether singleprofile is competitive is critical—if it is, it opens a new search axis; if not, we can confidently commit remaining budget to refining the multiprofile + transformer + weighted pipeline. It retains all the individually validated best components (top RNA encoder, top image encoder, best fusion) while probing the single largest untested design choice.

The evidence strongly identifies the optimal architecture as multimodal/multiprofile/transformer/weighted with imagenet_vit_l (config_039, acc 0.7250), and scvi_n200 clearly outperforms scgpt (0.72+ vs 0.52). However, pca_n2000 as an RNA encoder has never been tested in the multimodal setting, leaving an important uncertainty: whether a simpler linear representation could match or complement the learned scvi_n200 embedding when fused with the image modality. Config_029 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) isolates this single variable within the best-known architecture. If it underperforms scvi_n200 (likely), it confirms scvi_n200 is the right choice and we can confidently exploit the config_039 neighborhood in the remaining 3 experiments. If it performs comparably or better, it reveals a new direction. With only 3 experiments left, resolving this last major encoder uncertainty is the highest-value use of experiment 7 before committing the final budget to exploitation.

Evidence: The top-3 configurations all use scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer, with accuracy ranging 0.713–0.725. The current best (config_039: imagenet_vit_l, weighted) scores 0.725. Notably, config_013 (resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved the highest F1 (0.6945) despite lower accuracy, suggesting resnet50 captures complementary features. The only untested pairing of these proven-best components is resnet50 + concat fusion (config_001). This experiment tests whether the interaction between resnet50's feature space and concat fusion yields a synergistic gain over the current best. With only 2 experiments remaining after this, exploiting the strongest evidence (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) while filling the last gap in the 2×2 image-encoder × fusion grid is the highest-value use of this slot; if it underperforms, the remaining 2 experiments can confirm the ceiling or probe a different axis.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the best-performing region (config_039: 0.7250, config_021: 0.7207, config_004: 0.7062). The only untested configuration in this top region is config_017 (avgpool + concat), which completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid. While transformer+weighted is already the best, testing this remaining cell reduces residual uncertainty about whether the aggregation-fusion interaction could yield an unexpected result. Given that all other untested configs involve clearly inferior components (scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or image/rna-only), config_017 is the highest-value use of experiment 9: it either confirms the current best (config_039) or, in a small-probability case, reveals a new best for the final experiment to build upon.

The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 + multiprofile + multimodal as the best-performing family, with config_039 (imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) at 0.7250 as the current best. The only remaining untested configuration within this top family is config_027 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted). While avgpool has underperformed transformer for scvi_n200 (config_004: 0.7062 vs config_039: 0.7250), and resnet50 has been slightly weaker than imagenet_vit_l in accuracy (config_013: 0.7131), the weighted fusion consistently helps and resnet50 showed the highest F1 (0.6945) in the set, suggesting complementary discriminative strength. As the final experiment, config_027 completes the scvi_n200 multimodal multiprofile grid, provides the last opportunity to potentially exceed 0.7250 within the most promising design space, and confirms whether the imagenet_vit_l + transformer combination is truly optimal or whether a different pairing could marginally improve performance. All other untested configs involve scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or unimodal settings, all of which have shown substantially lower performance.
